name: ux-craft
description: Book-grounded UX engine for building, mocking and reviewing web and mobile UIs, forms, flows and emails — the UX brain that pairs with design-craft's visual hands. Three modes (Build / Review / Advise) over eleven references, and a deterministic gate that refuses what prose only asks: stdlib-only ux-lint.py runs static over HTML/JSX/CSS and probes a rendered page through Obscura, with every finding naming what you did, what the user silently gets, and the fix. Only exit 0 is a pass — a run that examined zero files refuses rather than reporting a clean sheet, and every run prints a never-empty not-checked list, because a check that cannot measure must say so instead of reporting zero. v2 resolves the accessibility floor against the standards themselves: 24x24 CSS px is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 at AA and is the only target-size number a WCAG failure may cite, 44x44 CSS px is SC 2.5.5 at AAA, and Apple's 44pt and Android's 48dp are craft targets in density-independent units that are not WCAG numbers at all. Twelve non-negotiables each carry the silent symptom that appears when they break, the state grid is a counted artifact rather than a rule that was read, and the destructive-action gate table, the probe-honesty rule and the model-family evidence taxonomy are available to every model rather than quarantined behind a model check. Carries a Known limits section, an evidence file rating the replication status of every behavioural law it cites (including the ones it argues against), the measured blind spots of the only sanctioned browser, and an autonomous-mode carve-out so a pipeline run is not told both to ask and not to ask.
